concept.title: Authority to Operate (ATO) for federal information systems
concept.shortdesc: An Authority to Operate (ATO) is the formal decision by a senior agency official to accept the security risk of running an information system. No federal system can go into production without one.

conbody.p: Every information system carries some risk. An ATO does not mean a system has no risk. It means an accountable official, called the authorizing official (AO), has reviewed the evidence and decided that the remaining risk is acceptable for the agency's mission.

section.title: Why an ATO matters
section.p: An ATO protects both the agency and the people whose data the system holds. Without one, a system cannot connect to agency networks or process government data. Losing an ATO can take a working system offline, so teams treat it as a continuing obligation rather than a one-time approval.

section.title: How a system earns an ATO
section.p: Most agencies follow the Risk Management Framework (RMF) in NIST Special Publication 800-37. The RMF has seven steps:

ol.li: Prepare. Set up roles, priorities, and the organization's risk strategy.
Categorize. Rate the impact (low, moderate, or high) if the system's confidentiality, integrity, or availability were lost.
Select. Choose security controls from NIST SP 800-53 that match that impact level.
Implement. Put the controls in place and document how each one works.
Assess. An independent assessor tests whether the controls work as described.
Authorize. The AO reviews the authorization package and grants, or denies, the ATO.
Monitor. The team tracks controls and changes continuously so the ATO stays valid.

section.title: What goes into an authorization package
section.p: The AO decides based on the authorization package, which usually contains three documents:

dlentry.dd: Describes the system and explains how each selected control is implemented.
Records the assessor's test results, including any controls that failed.
Lists each open weakness, who owns the fix, and when it is due.

section.title: Related terms
section.p: An Interim Authority to Test (IATT) allows limited testing before a full ATO. Continuous monitoring replaces the older model of reauthorizing every three years with ongoing checks.
